subject: science

concepts.title: Electric Cell Terminals
concepts.definition: An electric cell is a portable source of electricity that converts stored chemical energy into electrical energy, featuring two distinct ends called terminals.
concepts.key_idea: Cells have two poles, positive and negative, which drive current flow.
question_patterns: what are the terminals of an electric cell
identify the positive terminal of a cell
how many terminals does a cell have
where is the negative terminal located on a cell
describe electric cell terminals with an example

solution_steps.explain: The top metal cap is the positive terminal.
The bottom metal disc is the negative terminal.
When using the cell in a circuit, connect the positive cap and negative disc to opposite ends of the device so current can flow from positive to negative through the external path.

concepts.title: Bulb Structure and Filament
concepts.definition: An electric bulb produces light when current goes through a thin wire called a filament, which is supported by two terminals at the base.
concepts.key_idea: A bulb shines only when current completes a path through its filament.
question_patterns: what is the filament of a bulb
how are the terminals of a bulb arranged
why does a bulb have two terminals
what happens if the filament breaks
what do you understand by bulb structure and filament

solution_steps.explain: The filament is the thin wire inside the glass bulb.
If the filament is broken, the circuit is open and the bulb is fused.

Confirm that one terminal of the filament connects to the metal base case and the other to the central metal tip, so current can enter through one terminal, heat the filament, and leave through the other.

concepts.title: Electric Circuit Path
concepts.definition: An electric circuit is a continuous closed loop that allows electric current to flow from one terminal of a source to the other through a device.
concepts.key_idea: Current flows only in a complete, unbroken loop.
question_patterns: what is an electric circuit
why does the bulb glow in a closed circuit
what is the direction of current flow
define a complete path for electricity
explain electric circuit path in your own words

solution_steps.explain: Verify if the path connects positive to negative terminal.
If path is complete, current flows.

solution_steps.action: trace current direction through the loop
solution_steps.explain: Current leaves the positive terminal, travels through the bulb and connecting wires, and returns to the negative terminal; any break in this loop stops the flow and the bulb will not glow.

concepts.title: Electric Switch Function
concepts.definition: A switch is a mechanical device used to intentionally break or complete an electric circuit, thereby controlling the movement of current.
concepts.key_idea: A switch acts as a bridge that can be opened or closed.
question_patterns: what is the function of a switch
how does a switch control a bulb
what happens when a switch is in the off position
explain the working of a simple switch
what do you understand by electric switch function

solution_steps.explain: Determine if the switch connects the two points.
1 means circuit is closed, 0 means open.

solution_steps.action: relate switch position to bulb glow
solution_steps.explain: When the switch is in the on position it bridges the gap so current flows and the bulb glows; in the off position the gap breaks the loop, stopping current and turning the bulb off.

concepts.title: Conductors and Insulators
concepts.definition: Materials split by whether electric current can travel through them: current-passing ones are conductors, current-blocking ones are insulators.
concepts.key_idea: Conductors permit current flow; insulators prevent it.
question_patterns: distinguish between conductors and insulators
why are wires made of metal
is air a conductor or insulator
give examples of insulators used in daily life
explain conductors and insulators in your own words

solution_steps.explain: Check if current flows through the material.
If conducts is 1, it is a conductor.

Metals such as copper and aluminium are conductors that allow current to pass, while materials like rubber, plastic, and air are insulators that block current; this is why wires are metal coated with plastic insulation.
